findings.detail: scripts/agents-flow/notebook-auto-prune.sh line 575 uses grep -c piped then || echo 0. grep -c PRINTS 0 and EXITS 1 on no-match, so the || branch appends a SECOND 0. Command substitution therefore captures 0-newline-0, and the heredoc emits the sentinel_section_count key with value 0 followed by a newline and a stray 0-comma, which is invalid JSON. Fires precisely and only when the count is legitimately zero. Line 574 (NON_SENTINEL_SECTION_COUNT) carries the identical latent bug, currently masked because its count has been nonzero.
findings.evidence: 2 of 2 emitted files unparseable with byte-identical corruption: docs/signals/notebook-prune-dropped-newest-docs-agent-memory-notebooks-dev-mcp-server-md-2026-08-23T152548Z.json and the T194934Z sibling.
findings.impact: drain-signals.js line 220 catches the parse error, logs a stderr WARN, and leaves the file in the inbox forever (its own comment says it will re-warn every tick until removed at source). Both stuck signals are priority=high to claude-manager-helper, warning that the prune MAY HAVE DROPPED THE NEWEST notebook content. The safety signal for a destructive action is itself unreadable. It also makes any slurp-based consumer over docs/signals/*.json fail outright (jq -s exits 5).
findings.fix: replace the || echo 0 idiom with || true on BOTH lines 574 and 575 (grep -c already prints 0), then hand-repair or re-emit the 2 stuck files.

findings.detail: 6th consecutive cycle_snapshot_promoted=false. Step 4.7 names the file by wall-clock-at-write; emit_pressure_state looks it up by NOMINAL tick. Measured offset across 3 consecutive ticks this session: 05:15 to 05:17:03 (+2m03s), 05:30 to 05:33:19 (+3m19s), 05:45 to 05:48:46 (+3m46s). The offset is data-fetch latency and is always at least 2 minutes, so the wall-clock filename can essentially NEVER equal the nominal-tick key — even at drift_min=0, as this tick proves. Structural, not a race.
findings.distinct_from: The AGENT-side snapshot lookup is a DIFFERENT bug on the same filename scheme: the agent reads by its own wall-clock minute at read time and sometimes lands inside the same minute as the write (tally 5 hits / 6 misses). Two separate lookup defects — do not conflate them.
findings.also: cycle-snapshot-latest.json .tick is the bare string 00:00 while every per-tick writer emits a full ISO instant — a schema mismatch, so a consumer keying on .tick gets an unparseable value from latest. latest is now 29.7h stale (created_at 2026-08-23T00:07:50Z).
findings.fix: name the Step 4.7 file by NOMINAL tick, or use glob plus newest-by-created_at plus the existing 7-minute freshness check; ship both call sites together (.claude/skills/step-0-cowork/SKILL.md line 39 and .claude/skills/cycle-bootstrap/SKILL.md line 59).
